deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation. It is a working timetable, drafted twice, for the Göttingen mathematical-physical seminar (Wilhelm Weber's physical section), for one summer semester. The upper half is a pencil draft; the lower half is a cleaner ink revision.

Dating. The page can be dated to summer 1851 with near certainty, on four grounds:
- It refers to the solar eclipse of 28 July 1851 and to questions first raised by the eclipse of 8 July 1842.
- Every session date is a Thursday in 1851: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 May; 5, 12, 19, 26 June; 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 July; 7 Aug.
- 29 May 1851 was Ascension Day (Easter was 20 April 1851). This explains why the entry at '29' is a holiday note and not a session.
- The verso context, on both neighbouring pages, is drafts of Riemann's 1851 doctoral dissertation.

Schedule as reconstructed:
- 1 May (moved from 29 April): problems set; testing of the Mendelssohn balance.
- 8 May: demonstration of the cocoon-thread balance (a torsion/fibre balance), and determination of the weight in mg corresponding to a shift of the rider (Laufgewicht) by one scale division.
- 15 May: Young's modulus of brass from the tone of a sounding rod.
- 22 May: constants of the bifilar magnetometer.
- 30-31 May: magnetic term-day observations (Terminbeobachtungen, in the tradition of the Gauss-Weber Magnetic Union).
- 19 June: lecture on the theory of transverse vibrations of an elastic rod; problems set.
- 26 June: continuation of that lecture.
- 3 July: per the draft, something on the voltaic 'Spannungsreihe' (electrochemical tension series).
- 10 July: lecture by Ritter (referring back to 15 May), plus a report on the tension series.
- 17 July: Young's modulus from bending experiments, with telescope-and-scale reading.
- 24 July: lecture on the Mendelssohn balance; experiment on rates of cooling.
- 31 July (draft also gives 29 July): discussion of physical questions raised by the eclipse of 1842, prompted by that of 28 July 1851.
- 7 August: longitudinal and torsional vibrations of a string.
- Also listed: barometric measurement of the height of the Kleper (a hill near Göttingen), and 'Versuche an sehr dehnbaren [Körpern?]' (experiments on highly extensible bodies).

The names Hansen(?), Ritter and Riemann appear as speakers. This is consistent with Riemann's documented participation in, and assistant role at, Weber's seminar. The top line '6. 13. 20. 27. 3. 10. 17. 24.' is a list of weekly dates, perhaps for another term or weekday.

The only physics implicit is standard textbook material: the modulus from longitudinal tone, E = 4 rho L^2 f^2 for a free-free rod in its fundamental, and the Euler-Bernoulli theory of transverse rod vibrations. None of this is worked out on the page.
errors: No derivations, so no mathematical errors. Self-corrections in dating are visible: '19 April' is corrected to '19 Juni' in the 26 June entry, and 'Juli' is struck at the 3 July line. These are slips in a planning draft only.

results.what: Seminar programme: testing balances, Young's modulus of brass from the tone of a sounding rod and from bending, bifilar magnetometer constants, theory of transverse vibrations of elastic rods, longitudinal and torsional vibrations of a string, barometric height measurement, cooling rate, voltaic tension series, eclipse questions
results.modern_name: Standard 19th-century experimental physics exercises (acoustic determination of Young's modulus, Euler-Bernoulli beam vibrations, bifilar magnetometer)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (rod vibrations, 18th c.), Chladni (tone methods), Gauss and Weber (bifilar magnetometer, 1830s)

results.what: Documentary evidence that Riemann (also writing his dissertation then) took part in, and helped organise, Weber's mathematical-physical seminar in summer 1851
results.usually_credited_to: Known from Dedekind's biography of Riemann and the seminar records

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative seminar timetable with no mathematics. It confirms the known fact that Riemann was involved in Weber's physics seminar around 1850-51. Its main value is minor archival dating: it is a Thursday schedule for summer 1851, written on the back of dissertation drafts.

checkable.asserts: 1 May 1851 was a Thursday, so the weekly session dates on the page are all Thursdays of 1851

checkable.sympy: import datetime; all(d.weekday()==3 for d in [datetime.date(1851,5,8),datetime.date(1851,5,15),datetime.date(1851,5,22),datetime.date(1851,6,19),datetime.date(1851,6,26),datetime.date(1851,7,3),datetime.date(1851,7,10),datetime.date(1851,7,17),datetime.date(1851,7,24),datetime.date(1851,7,31),datetime.date(1851,8,7)])
checkable.asserts: All listed session dates fall on Thursday in 1851

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; from datetime import date, timedelta; from dateutil.easter import easter; easter(1851)+timedelta(days=39)==date(1851,5,29)
checkable.asserts: 29 May 1851 was Ascension Day, explaining the gap at '29' in the draft

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; E,rho,L,f=symbols('E rho L f',positive=True); simplify(sqrt(E/rho)/(2*L) - f).subs(E,4*rho*L**2*f**2)==0
checkable.asserts: Fundamental longitudinal frequency of a free-free rod is f=sqrt(E/rho)/(2L), so E=4 rho L^2 f^2 (the 'Elasticitätsmodulus aus dem Tone eines Klangstabes' method; standard, not written on the page)

transcription_corrections: Line '8 [Mai] Coconfadenwage': in the pencil draft the second line reads 'Coconfadenwage' (cocoon-thread balance), placed between the 1 May and 15 May entries.

'29 Termin[?] 5. 12. 19' is more plausibly '29 Himmelf.' (Ascension Day, 29 May 1851), followed by the next dates 5, 12 (19 struck). The '30' line likely marks the term-day observations of 30-31 May, as the ink list confirms.
In the 17 July line, 'Fernrohr und Scale' refers to telescope-and-scale (Poggendorff-Gauss) reading for the bending experiment.
In the 24 July line, the pencil reads 'Versuch über die Abkühlungsgeschwindigkeit' (rate of cooling). The struck words before it are probably 'Gesetz der Abk[ühlung]'.
The 7 Aug ink entry reads 'Longitudinal- und Torsionsschwingungen einer Saite'. 'Demonstration' is struck beneath it.

The 8 May ink entry reads 'Demonstration der Coconfadenwage. Bestimmung des [Gewichtes] in mgr. welcher einer Verschiebung des Laufgew. um 1 Scalentheil entspricht'. The text '... Werthes einer Verschiebung des Laufgewichts um einen Scalentheil' at the right belongs to this 8 May entry, not to 7 Aug.
'Kleper' is the hill (Kleperberg) near Göttingen; the reading 'Höhe der Kleper' is plausible.
The 31 July entry: 'Erörterung einiger durch die Sonnenfinsterniss von 1842 angeregter physikalischer Fragen, aus Anlass der Sonnenfinsterniss v. 28. Juli', with '(29. Juli)' as an alternative date.
